Categories.value: Field recording|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Wingtip vortices|Sounds of air transport

ImageDescription.value: Excerpt from a field recording that I took at Berlin Tegel Airport in June 2011, standing next to the Western airport fence where the airplanes fly over landing (if there is easterly wind). The sound of the airplane is quite intense. However, the crucial part of this recording starts at 50 seconds: closely following the direct noise of the airplane you can hear the subtle sound of the wake vortex (or: wing tip vortex, which is a trail of turbulent air behind an airplane). The wake vortex creates a flimsy swish and rustle. However, its sound is not always so articulate and continuous as it was this time. It lasts from 0’50 to the end of the recording.

ObjectName.value: "Motor Boat Rag" by Henry W. Gaul (1911)

Categories.value: Media from YouTube|PD-old-75-expired|CC-PD-Mark|Uploaded with video2commons|PD-old missing SDC copyright status

ImageDescription.value:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/12780610?from=youtube_share 
How come every rag that originates anywhere near Cincinnati turns out to be "a good rag"? This obscure rag from nearby Newport, Kentucky is no exception. Published by Tropwen Music Co. in Newport in 1911. It's the only findable work by musician Henry William Gaul, who lived from 1895 to 1947 and is buried in Cincinnati, Ohio.

Original score source was from Walter Cosand at this link (copy/paste entire URL if needed): http://waltercosand.com/CosandScores/Composers%20E-K/Gaul , %20Henry%20W/Gaul-Motor_Boat_Rag.pdf

This is a reproduction of the original score with a few amendments. Added repeat bars to the Trio (because it's a nice trio); changed the note durations at measures 13 and 46 so they make sense; added various missing accidentals in the B and C strains, most notably to all the Bs in measure 60; deleted the left-hand Es in measure 68.

ObjectName.value: 20 years of Wikimania — Wikimania Village Pump — Wikimania 2025 in Nairobi, Kenya

Categories.value: Wikimania 2025 Village Pump podcast

ImageDescription.value:
The 2025 iteration of the Wikimania conference held in Nairobi served as a venue for documenting the history of this event over the past two decades. Participants gathered at the Trademark Hotel to discuss the evolution of the conference since its inception in Frankfurt during 2005. Early organizers noted that the initial gathering focused on bringing members of the community together for the first time in a dedicated space. These early events involved logistical challenges such as managing internet connectivity and securing venues within the constraints of limited budgets and volunteer support

Various speakers reflected on the shifting nature of the conference locations and the logistical requirements of hosting attendees. The transition from informal settings such as youth hostels to professional conference facilities mirrored the growth of the Wikimedia movement. Organizers from different years shared personal anecdotes regarding their experiences with site selection and the collaborative efforts required to manage international logistics. The discussion highlighted how the process of selecting host cities changed as the organization matured and adopted more structured planning methods.

Specific editions of the conference were noted for their distinct impact on the broader movement. The 2008 event in Alexandria was cited for its focus on the relationship between libraries and the Wikimedia project. This period saw the development of partnerships between these institutions and the movement. Participants also recalled the technical difficulties and the resourcefulness required to maintain operations in various environments, emphasizing that local community involvement was a factor in the success of these gatherings..

The 2011 event in Haifa was mentioned for its role in the development of Wikidata, which emerged from connections made during that specific conference. Speakers noted that regional collaboration became a recurring theme as the organization looked for ways to support community members across different geographical areas. This period marked a transition in how the foundation interacted with local organizers, with more emphasis placed on long term planning and the inclusion of diverse perspectives from various regions.

Recent editions of the conference incorporated hybrid models to address global accessibility and the constraints imposed by external events. The transition to online formats during the pandemic allowed the movement to maintain engagement while planning for the resumption of in person gatherings. The experience in Singapore and the subsequent regional collaboration models demonstrated the feasibility of hosting events that combined local participation with remote access. This shift enabled broader attendance from regions that previously faced difficulties with international travel..

Looking toward the future, organizers discussed the ongoing efforts to maintain the inclusive nature of the movement. The closing remarks emphasized the importance of volunteers and the role of the conference as a platform for sharing knowledge across different languages and cultures. Reflections on the history of the event served to underline the commitment of participants to the core goals of the Wikimedia movement. The documentation of these two decades provided a context for the continued evolution of the community and the planning of upcoming sessions.

ImageDescription.value: Teams at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Oct. 21, 2026, on the Fred Haise Test Stand. The hot fire test lasted for almost eight-and-a-half minutes (500 seconds), the same amount of time RS-25 engines fire during launch of NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket, with a 111% power level. The main objectives of the test were to acceptance test RS-25 flight components for future Artemis missions and validate the new thermal protection system, which protects the RS-25 engine nozzle from the thermal environment surrounding SLS during launch. While this developmental engine will not be used in flight, the hot fire test provides NASA and NASA’s prime engine contractor L3Harris Technologies with the capability to capture critical data to improve engine performance and reliability. Prior to use, all RS-25 engines are proven flightworthy at NASA Stennis. For each Artemis mission, four RS-25 engines produce up to 2 million pounds of combined thrust to help launch the SLS rocket.

ImageDescription.value:
A video, realisateur-bouba-kams from Cote D'Ivoire for Wiki Loves Africa 2024. This video focuses on the entrepreneurial journey of Ms. Marie Chantal Kouassi, founder and director of the company macKen Concept, during the construction process of the headquaters of Genesis Holding Company, from land acquisition to construction and finishing of the building. Genesis Holding Company is an ivorian company specialized in financial intermediation; the provision of technical studies, market studies, business plans, etc.; business development, particularly through direct financing, equity participation, joint ventures, etc.; and lobbying with private and public, national or international organizations.
As for macKen Concept, the company is a real estate company for the construction of buildings, offices and housing. The company is located in Abidjan, Cocody Synacassi 2 (Ivory Coast). It also offers the development and renovation of buildings and spaces (interior design and decoration and other green spaces, etc.). macKen Concept is an SARL created and managed by Mrs. Marie Chantal Kouassi, an Ivorian entrepreneur.

ImageDescription.value: A Windows media player file containing a movie showing alveolar instability in the nondependent low PEEP group 60 minutes following injurious ventilation. At end expiration there is a great deal of atelectasis, which appears as dark-red areas without the presence of alveolar structures. During inspiration, the collapsed alveoli reach the critical opening pressure and 'pop' open. When the critical closing pressure is reached during exhalation, the alveoli collapse. The mechanism of this collapse and re-expansion appears to be by alveolar folding and unfolding (Figure 5).

ImageDescription.value: Crews at NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans transport the 130-foot-tall liquid hydrogen tank from the proof testing building to the main factory on July 15. The liquid hydrogen tank will form part of the core stage for the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket for the agency’s Artemis IV mission, providing thousands of gallons of super-cold propellant to the rocket engines during launch. Soon, teams with SLS prime contractor, Boeing, will move the tank into the facility’s vertical assembly building for cleaning operations. The liquid hydrogen propellant tank is one of five major elements that make up the 212-foot-tall SLS rocket stage. The core stage, along with its four RS-25 engines at its base, produce more than two million pounds of thrust to help launch NASA’s Orion spacecraft, astronauts, and supplies beyond Earth’s orbit and to the lunar surface for Artemis.

Categories.value: PD NASA|Files with closed captioning in English|Uploaded with video2commons|Video display resolution 3840 x 2160|NASA videos in 2026|Files from NASA with known IDs|NASA Library files uploaded by OptimusPrimeBot|Artemis 4 core stage|Artemis 4 at Michoud Assembly Facility|4K NASA videos

ImageDescription.value: The Artemis IV core stage’s boat tail section is lifted and moved from its production area at NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans on Aug. 24, 2026. The boat tail refers to the aerodynamic portion positioned directly above the exposed RS-25 engine nozzles, which comprise the lower portions of the core stage’s engine section. The boat tail critically shields the rocket’s lowermost hardware, including the engines’ upper components, plumbing, and critical control systems, protecting them from the extreme heat, vibrations, and pressures during launch. The completed hardware is lifted via the factory’s overhead crane system and secured onto two self-propelled modular transporters—NASA’s mobile heavy transport platforms,—for a short, low-speed drive across the facility, from the factory to the Pegasus barge. From New Orleans, the hardware travels to Kennedy Space Center for future engine section integration, and eventual stacking following the Artemis III mission. Through the Artemis campaign, NASA will send astronauts to explore the Moon for scientific discovery, economic benefits, and to build the foundation for the first crewed missions to Mars—for the benefit of all.

ImageDescription.value:
Automatic butt-welding machine

Butt welding is a welding technique used to connect parts which are nearly parallel and don't overlap. Butt-welding is an economical and reliable way of joining without using additional components. Butt-welding joint is made by gradually heating up the two weld ends with a weld plate and then joining them under a specific pressure.

This machine was built 1926 in Köln, Germany.

Killebergs Kettingfabrik

In 1905 Otto Jönsson built a workshop in Killeberg and started chain manufacturing in smaller scale. Belt driven full - and semiautomatic machines procured the chain. New products were developed, like the "Killeberg chain" where each link is turned 45 degrees and therefore protects the animals' necks. The factory was in operation until 2002 and a year later Loshult local history society bought the factory and turned it into a Work life museum.

ObjectName.value: Automatic robotic lawn mower Gardena Sileno City 250 in action

Categories.value: Robotic lawn mowers in Germany|Self-published work|Robotic lawn mowers by Gardena|Videos of robotic lawn mowers

ImageDescription.value:
AUDIO WARNING: At about 1:35 (1 minute 35 seconds), there is a very loud noise because someone in the neighbourhood threw some metallic things on concrete, or the like. So beware to turn the audio level up too much, at least at this position of the video.

Automatic robotic lawn mower Gardena Sileno City 250 (model also known or renamed as Minimo) in action. The mower is basically a model from Husqvarna sold under the Gardena brand. During parts of the video, a black thin line can be seen which extends straight across the garden area. This is a part of the "orientation" or guidance lines which have to be installed prior to first operation of the mower. They extend mainly at the physical outer borders of the lawn (e.g. in front of the bushes in the back), so that the robot can calculate where to turn around. The cables carry very weak electrical alternating current (or pulsed) signals (voltage unknown to the author, but probably not more than about 15 Volts), which are received by the robot via an antenna when approaching the lawn border.

ImageDescription.value:
Kenya Defence Forces service members conduct helicopter landing zone operations at the Counter Insurgency Terrorism and Stability Operations centre during exercise Justified Accord 2025 (JA25) in Nanyuki, Kenya, Feb. 19, 2025. JA25 is the premier U.S. Africa Command (USAFRICOM) exercise in East Africa, designed to enhance multinational combat readiness, strengthen crisis response capabilities and empower allies and partners in the region. Led by U.S. Army Southern European Task Force, Africa (SETAF-AF) and hosted by Kenya, Djibouti and Tanzania, JA25 integrates high-intensity training scenarios that sharpen warfighting skills, increase operational reach and enhance the ability to execute complex joint and multinational operations. The exercise runs from Feb. 10–21, 2025. (U.S. Air Force video by Tech. Sgt. Anastasia Tompkins)

U.S. Soldiers assigned to the 173rd Airborne Brigade practice sequences on a .50-caliber machine gun lane before testing on the weapon lane at Grafenwöhr Training Area, Grafenwöhr, Sept. 19, 2025. ImageDescription.value:
U.S. Soldiers operate an unmanned aircraft system during African Lion 26 at Southern Zone Headquarters, Agadir, Morocco, April 30, 2026. The exercise gave service members an opportunity to test AI-powered and autonomous platforms, remote systems, and emerging technologies across attack, defense and mission command operations. The experimentation accelerated target detection, shortened decision timelines and delivered cost-effective warfighting solutions aligned with African partner priorities. 
AL26 is U.S. Africa Command's largest annual joint exercise, designed to strengthen collective security capabilities of the U.S., African nations and global allies. ImageDescription.value:
Yes, it's not played by me, but my student Siming, He. After getting his parents and his own permission, and after one month's exercises in classroom, I can submit this piece.

Siming, He (Chinese characteristics-meaning of his name: Like a lively sculpture, this clever boy is from He family), was a very lively and extroverted boy. He has many interests and talents, such English, hosting, reciting poems, Go-playing... Therefore, it's very hard to let him focus the attention onto piano and make a steady and silent song, through the soft and restless little hands... Thanks to his parents' association. We did succeed...When playing this tune, he almost changed to another person - calming down the breathes and making out some very graceful actions... like a real boatman, musically boating for us... in a lazy afternoon.

Regarding with the information of its composer - Bach... sorry, I am seeking for my textbook. It's said this tune was from an opera; and this Bach wasn't piano-kids' familiar Baroque Bach... I need to do some researches...

All in all, let us listen to him

ObjectName.value: Booster Demonstration Motor-1 Static Test at Northrop Grumman (MSFC-NG-06262025 DM-1 Static Test at Northrop Grumman)

Categories.value: PD NASA|Northrop Grumman|Files with closed captioning in English|Uploaded with video2commons|Video display resolution 3840 x 2160|Videos of 2025 from the United States|NASA videos in 2025|Files from NASA with known IDs|NASA Library files uploaded by OptimusPrimeBot|Videos taken on 2025-06-26|Booster Obsolescence Life Extension|4K NASA videos

ImageDescription.value: Northrop Grumman conducted the first test firing of its Booster Obsolescence and Life Extension (BOLE) five-segment solid rocket motor at its Promontory production and test site in Utah. The Development Motor 1 (DM-1) fired Thursday, June 26, at 12:25 PM MDT (18:25 UTC) and lasted for close to two minutes and 20 seconds, burning over 1.4 million pounds of propellant. The BOLE motor is intended for use on the Block 2 version of NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket, beginning with the Artemis IX mission. Featuring unpainted composite casings with copper wiring wrapped around them for protection against lightning, the booster generated over 4 million pounds of thrust upon ignition and burned for approximately two minutes and 20 seconds. Sensors monitored hundreds of parameters using 763 channels of data, and a carbon dioxide quench system helped to safe the booster after its firing. The BOLE DM-1 motor turned out to be the second most powerful solid rocket motor ever tested, behind only a 260 inch booster in the 1960s. The motor, mounted on its side, was held down by a large concrete block, which prevents it from moving forward. All test motors for the program are processed in an assembly building enclosure that is moved away from the motor prior to the test.

ImageDescription.value: This video follows the cross-country journey of eight of the 10 solid rocket booster segments that will help power NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket for the Artemis III mission. Transported by rail from Northrop Grumman’s facility in Corinne, Utah, to NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida, the shipment marked the first trip for Union Pacific Railroad’s newest commemorative locomotive, No. 4547. Midway through the journey, the booster segments were transferred to another rail carrier, Norfolk Southern, to complete their trip to Florida. The 10 booster motor segments will be assembled into the SLS rocket’s twin solid rocket boosters, which provide more than 75% of the vehicle’s thrust at liftoff. For more information about SLS, visit https://www.nasa.gov/sls.

ObjectName.value: Chicago Photographed from Ray Knabenshue's Dirigible Air Ship (enhanced)

Categories.value: A. Roy Knabenshue|Aerial views of Chicago|PD US expired|PD-US missing SDC copyright status|Videos of airships

ImageDescription.value:
Chicago Photographed from Ray Knabenshue's Dirigible Air Ship
The first successful passenger dirigible flight in the United States
National Archives Identifier: 95608
Local Identifier: KNAB-KNAB-201 https://catalog.archives.gov/id/95608
From: Series: Motion Picture Film, 1914 - 1914
Collection: Roy Knabenshue Collection, 1914 - 1914
This item was produced or created: 1914
Scope & Content: On the first successful passenger dirigible flight in the United States. Shows the dirigible leaving its hangar, ascending, in flight, and being berthed. Aerial views of Chicago include suburban residential districts, parkways around the city, public beaches, harbor scenes, golf courses, railroad yards, downtown office buildings, and tenement districts.

Contact(s): National Archives at College Park - Motion Pictures (RDSM) National Archives at College Park 8601 Adelphi Road College Park, MD 20740-6001 Phone: 301-837-3540

On June 17, 1914, Ray Knabenshue's dirigible White City made its first Chicago flight, a 24-minute trip over the city’s parks and Lake Michigan with eight passengers aboard.
It flew for an hour and a half on June 26. “The airship left White City shortly after 4 o’clock,” Aero and Hydro reported. “Within 30 minutes it had passed Twelfth Street. It followed the lakeshore and turned loopward just north of Grant Park. It circled over many of the famous skyscrapers, and the seven passengers looked down into the ‘wells’ of the big buildings. A photographer in the dirigible took a number of views during the trip.”
The passengers that day were four women, two men and, in the back, a movie camera operator. It wasn’t unusual for movie cameramen to be called “photographers” at that time—films were “reels of pictures.” White City flew low and slow and the cameraman took clear footage of buildings, ships, railyards, automobiles and people, and of the airship being taken out of its shed and put back into it. This film eventually vanished into the National Archives and was only recently rediscovered there by Chicago Tribune reporters.

ObjectName.value: Czech Jewish children evacuated via airplane (1939)

Categories.value: Nicholas Winton|Newsreels|Kindertransporte|Files from external sources with reviewed licenses|1939-01-11|PD-anon-70-EU|Videos of 1939|Uploaded with video2commons|Jewish children in World War II|Children with aircraft

ImageDescription.value:
As part of Kindertransport, Czech Jewish children board an airplane at Ruzyně airport, Prague, Czechoslovakia, which will take them to safety in London. Sir Nicholas Winton appears towards the end of the clip, wearing glasses.

>From a contemporary news report: "Today on the aerodrome of Ruzyn nearly 30 children of refugees took leave of their parents. Two Dutch Douglas airplanes brought them to Rotterdam and from there to London. This is the charitable work of the Barbican Mission of London, under direction of Rev. Wallner. He intends to give 60 children all together a new home in London where they will remain till their 18th year. The youngest of these children is only two and a half years old, the eldest one 11 years old. The leave-taking was grievous. Nobody was untouched seeing the tears of the remaining parents who will not see again their children for many long years. Before starting the pilot said: 'Never my life I have had such a responsibility. My Lord -- 30 children!' Five hours later I get the news that the airplanes are well landed in London."

ImageDescription.value: Bioscoopjournaals waarin Nederlandse onderwerpen van een bepaalde week worden gepresenteerd.; In Numansdorp, waar de grond na de Watersnoodramp weer drooggevallen maar nog steeds erg drassig is, wordt een demonstratie gegeven van een tractor die speciaal gemaakt is voor moerassige terreinen. De tractor, uitgerust met brede rupsbanden ipv wielen, trekt makkelijk een zware greppelploeg door de natte grond. Medewerkers van Rijkswaterstaat en de Heidemaatschappij, bedacht op herstel van de schade in de rampgebieden, kijken zeer geïnteresseerd toe.

Categories.value: PD US|The Dog Factory|WebM videos|Videos from Edison Manufacturing|Videos from the Library of Congress|Video display resolution 320 x 240|Videos uploaded by Racconish

ImageDescription.value: American short silent film. From Edison's catalog : "On the walls of the factory a lot of different varieties of frankfurters are hung. Each is marked with the breed of dog it is made from. A combined dog and bologna making machine is seen in the foreground, and two Germans are working industriously over it. A tramp enters with about a dozen dogs of various types, and sells them to the Germans. They are soon transformed into sausage and the tramp departs with his cash. A dude now enters who wants to buy a spaniel. The dog is quickly made and sold. A number of customers follow and are supplied with dogs that suit their fancies. Finally a tough enters who wants a bull dog. A Boston Bull is produced, but does not suit him. He wants a fighting bull. The dog is made, and as he jumps from the machine he grabs the tough by the pants, and dog and man mix up in a rolling match all over the floor. The tough finally releases himself and disappears, leaving the fighting bull dog to be again turned into bologna. 240 ft. $36.00."

ObjectName.value: Die Dülkener Narrenakademie. Verleihung des Doktorgrades hum

Categories.value: Videos of 1975 from Germany|Media from YouTube|Narrenmühle|LVR-Institut für Landeskunde und Regionalgeschichte|Uploaded with video2commons|License reviewed by YouTubeReviewBot|Videos in German|Gabriel Simons

ImageDescription.value:
Die Dülkener Narrenakademie. Verleihung des Doktorgrades hum c und Narrenritt um die Mühle

Dülken 1975 – 28 min Aufnahme: Gabriel Simons; Kommentar: Susanne Bilo

Die Senatoren der Dülkener Narrenakademie kommen in der Narrenmühle zusammen um einem ausgewählten Kandidaten das Diplom "Doctor humoris causa" zu verleihen. Gerade einmal drei Fragen müssen beantwortet werden, um die Doktorwürden zu erlangen. Der Haken dabei: Selbst die gründlichste wissenschaftliche Vorbereitung nützt nichts, denn die drei Fragen sind Scherzfragen. Bei Bestehen der Prüfung wird dem ausgewählten Kandidaten dieser „Doctor humoris causa“ verliehen. Jetzt kann mit drei Hammerschlägen gegen die Mühlentür und einem Steckenpferdritt um die Mühle das närrische Jahr eröffnet werden.

ImageDescription.value:
Table of content:

00:11 Stepper motor 01:27 Shortening the turn-on time 02:16 Enabling inductors simultaneously 03:19 Altering the direction of rotation 04:29 Software modes stepper motor 06:37 Rotation by repelling forces 09:04 Sensor disc 09:29 Electronic commutation 11:07 Brake pedal 11:31 Automatic speed control 12:33 Revolution counter 14:59 Electric input power 17:33 Losses at the power transistors (temperature) 18:28 Mechanical output power (efficiency) 19:28 Software modes commutated motor 22:48 Oscillograph turn-on times

The functionality of an electric motor is treated at this video. The motor is converted from a stepper motor into an electronically commutated motor in progress of the film. In addition, the efficiency of the motor is determined. To do so, the electric input power and the mechanical output power are measured. The used materials of the electric motor are as simple as possible to be able to do a reverse engeneering. The functionality is demonstrated by using a self-made revolution counter, digital multimeter, LEDs and an oscilloscope. An ATmega8A microcontroller is used to control the motor by software.

This little electric motor is a test model of an electric vehicle, which is built as an open source project by now.

ObjectName.value: Earth from Orbit- Cargo Ship Backup Seen from Space (NESDIS 2021-04-02)

Categories.value: PD US NOAA|Uploaded with video2commons|Video display resolution 3840 x 2160|2021 satellite pictures|Videos of satellite pictures of Earth|NESDIS files uploaded by OptimusPrimeBot|Photos by VIIRS (Suomi NPP)|Photos by VIIRS (NOAA-20)|Satellite pictures of 2021 Suez Canal obstruction

ImageDescription.value: After an international team worked for six days and nights dredging sand to free a giant container ship blocking the Suez Canal, the high spring tide from a super moon finally helped set the Ever Given free. The quarter-mile-long ship, which had become wedged in muck and clay along the banks of the canal, was “refloated” at about 3 pm local time Monday, and tugboat horns blared in celebration. In the early hours of March 29, Day Night Band imagery from the NOAA-20 satellite was able to capture images of the more than 400 ships backed up on both sides of the operation, in the Red Sea and Bitter Lake. And 100 percent illumination from the moon allowed for clear images of the land and water features. Because of the high spring tide, which occurs when the Earth, Sun and Moon are in alignment, water rose about 18 inches above normal levels. The Day-Night Band is part of the Suomi-NPP and NOAA-20 satellites’ VIIRS instrument. In the dark, the human eye dilates to allow in more light, and this improves night vision. Similarly, the Day-Night Band instrument sees a broad spectrum of light ranging in wavelengths from green at 500 nanometers to near infrared at 900 nanometers. Due to the wide spectrum, the sensor is highly sensitive to light. With filtering techniques, the Day-Night Band can also distinguish between city lights, moonlight, auroras and other light sources, such as light from ships.

Credit.value: Earth from Orbit: Cargo Ship Backup Seen from Space

ObjectName.value: EU–Lithuania Association Council. Round table and extracts from the press conference (I-027272)

Categories.value: Hans-Friedrich von Ploetz|Relations of the European Union and Lithuania|Information field template with formatting|Videos of 1999 from Luxembourg|Hans van den Broek in 1999|EC-Audiovisual Center review needed|Algirdas Saudargas|Media from the European Commission|Videos by the European Commission|Videos taken on 1999-02-22

ImageDescription.value: On 22 February 1999, the meeting of the EU/Lithuania Association Council took place in Luxembourg. The Lithuanian delegation was headed by Algirdas Saudargas, Lithuanian Minister for Foreign Affairs. The European Union was represented by Hans-Friedrich von Ploetz, German Federal State Secretary for Foreign Affairs and President-in-office of the Council, and by Hans van den Broek, Member of the EC in charge of External Relations with the Countries of Central and Eastern Europe, the former Soviet Union, Mongolia, Turkey, Cyprus, Malta and other European Countries, Common Foreign and Security Policy and Human Rights (in agreement with the President) and External Missions. The meeting enabled the two sides to take stock of Lithuania's progress in the pre-accession strategy in the light of the Accession Partnership and the Commission's first regular report, and to review bilateral relations under the Europe Agreement. There was also an exchange of views on international issues of common interest. This meeting was followed by a press conference. Hans van den Broek outlined that the conclusion of the meeting of the Association Council indicated the progress made by Lithuania despite its position close to Russia and its economic crisis. Algirdas Saudargas expressed his satisfaction and his wish to see his country back at the negotiating table with the EU as soon as possible.

ImageDescription.value: Occurrence of CNRs. IR monitoring of experimental “nest 02” (cf. Fig 1) through 33 min at 3.9427 Hz. The temperature scale on the right is fixed between 26° and 40°C, whereby the range of the actual temperature pixels is displayed by the small bar between the scale partition and the rainbow-900 palette. The black bar at the bottom displays the relative time of the image noted in minutes. The blue-green areas represent CNRs while the tiny red spots regard to the interstices between the bees of the surface layer; according to the ventilation hypothesis they document the “exhalation” phase when nest-warm air is pressed out through the diffuse mesh of the curtain (cf. Fig 7).

ImageDescription.value: Fanning bee at a CNR. In the quiescent region of the bee curtain, peripheral to the mouth zone [6–8, 12], most of the bees are positioned in a vertical body alignment, with heads up and abdomens down. However, some bees display postures with the head pointing away from the vertical surface of the nest. These bees are potential fanners, most of them were identified near or at CNRs. This bee displayed in the mid of the image was fanning throughout nearly the entire observation session (cf. Fig 6, panel A).

ObjectName.value: EsLibre2020 18V.P2.02 - Álvaro del Castillo San Félix - Creación de juegos 2D-3D con Godot Engine

Categories.value: Self-published work|EsLibre 2020|Eventos OfiLibre

ImageDescription.value:
[esLibre 2020] Viernes 18 - Pista II

Título: "Creación de juegos 2D/3D con Godot Engine"

Ponente: Álvaro del Castillo San Félix

En la pasada edición de esLibre presentó el taller de big data.

Resumen:

Godot Engine es un motor de creación de juegos 2D/3D Open Source que compite en la actualidad con los motores líderes en el mercado: Unity y Unreal. Con Godot se están creando juegos profesionales en todos los ámbitos del mercado y para todas las plataformas. Su desarrollo durante más de 10 años ha alcanzado una madurez que le está dando una gran popularidad en la actualidad.

Godot proporciona metodologías, un entorno integrado completo, un lenguaje de scripting que simplifica la programación, APIs, integración con motor de física Bullet, documentación y una comunidad amplia (más de 1000 contribuidores en GitHub) para ayudar en la creación de juegos 2D/3D profesionales, que funcionan en Linux, Windows, Android, iOS o Web entre otros.

Durante el taller el objetivo es conocer el proyecto, el editor donde se crean los juegos, su lenguaje de scripting de programación (GDScript) y el desarrollo de un juego 2D basado en el tutorial oficial de Godot pero con evoluciones que ha terminado en el juego Open Source “Numbers Attack”: https://github.com/acs/numbers_attack. El final del taller será la creación de versiones para Linux, Web y Android del juego.

Más información: https://propuestas.eslib.re/2020/talleres/creacion-juegos-godot-engine

Programa completo del congreso: https://eslib.re/2020/programa/

Categories.value: Images with extracted images|Information field template with formatting|Göran Persson in 1999|Videos of 1999 from Finland|EC-Audiovisual Center review needed|Media from the European Commission|Videos by the European Commission|Videos taken on 1999-12-11|1999 European Council in Helsinki|Anna Lindh in 1999

ImageDescription.value: On 11 December 1999, Göran Persson, Swedish Prime Minister, held a press briefing following the 2-day meeting of the Heads of State or Government of the EU Member States in Helsinki (Finland). The meeting was chaired by Paavo Tapio Lipponen, Finnish Prime Minister, and attended by Romano Prodi, President of the EC. The proceedings were rounded off by a meeting with representatives of the 13 candidate countries seeking membership of the European Union. The European Council adopted the 'Millennium declaration', a common strategy on Ukraine and a declaration on Chechnya. It decided to begin accession negotiations with Romania, Slovakia, Latvia, Lithuania, Bulgaria and Malta, and to recognise Turkey as a candidate country, thereby marking a new stage in the enlargement process. It also decided to convene, in February 2000, an intergovernmental conference for revising the Treaties, which was expected to complete its work by December 2000. Other decisions taken were aimed at strengthening the common European security and defence policy, by developing military and civilian crisis management capabilities, with particular emphasis on launching and conducting EU-led military operations in response to international crises. Furthermore, the employment guidelines for 2000 were approved, along with recommendations to the Member States concerning implementation of their employment policies.

ImageDescription.value: On 11 December 1999, Bülent Ecevit, Turkish Prime Minister, held a press conference following his meeting with the European Council, in Helsinki (Finland). The day before, the Council decided to begin accession negotiations with Romania, Slovakia, Latvia, Lithuania, Bulgaria and Malta, and to recognise Turkey as a candidate country, thereby marking a new stage in the enlargement process. The same day, in the evening, Javier Solana, Secretary-General of the Council and High Representative for Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP), and Günter Verheugen, Member of the EC in charge of Enlargement, went to Ankara (Turkey) to inform the Turkish Government about the decision of the Council. During the press conference, Bülent Ecevit outlined that the declaration of Turkey as a candidate country, on equal footing with other candidate countries in an unequivocal manner and with clarity, was a positive development, opening the road for Turkey's full membership. He also presented the important position of Turkey as a crossroad of continents, regions, religions, modernity and traditions. He also shared his view on the abolition of capital punishment in the country.

Categories.value: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 missing SDC copyright license|Creative Commons Attribution missing SDC copyright status|Events/celebrations music from Filmmusic|Advertising music from Filmmusic|Sports music from Filmmusic|Cinematic (genre) music from Filmmusic|Cinematic (topic) music from Filmmusic|Adventure music from Filmmusic|Intros music from Filmmusic|Countries/travel music from Filmmusic

ImageDescription.value:
Alright, let's talk about "Epic Drone Shots 001." From the first few bars, this track immediately establishes itself as a high-quality, professionally crafted cinematic piece. It opens with a sense of anticipation, using pulsing strings and a subtle, underlying tension that hints at something significant about to unfold. This isn't just background noise; it's designed to elevate visuals and evoke a strong emotional response.

The instrumentation is primarily orchestral, featuring lush, sweeping string arrangements that provide the core emotional weight. They glide effortlessly, creating a feeling of soaring motion – perfectly aligning with its (implied, based on the title) suitability for aerial footage, sweeping landscapes, or grand reveals. The string writing is effective, utilizing both legato lines for smoothness and staccato bursts for rhythmic drive and emphasis, particularly as the track builds.

Percussion plays a crucial role here, entering assertively to inject energy and momentum. It’s not overly complex but serves its purpose perfectly, providing a solid, driving foundation that propels the track forward. Think powerful timpani rolls and crisp snare patterns that punctuate the string melodies and build intensity towards the key climactic moments. There might be subtle synth pads layered underneath, adding a touch of modern breadth and warmth, but the overall feel remains firmly rooted in the contemporary orchestral/cinematic sound.

Structurally, the piece follows a familiar but highly effective arc common in production music: intro, build-up, climax, and resolution. It understands its role – to support a narrative. The gradual layering of instruments and dynamics creates a compelling journey. It starts with promise, gathers steam, hits a powerful peak perfect for showcasing a key moment or message, and then often resolves satisfyingly, though this one maintains high energy for a good portion.

In terms of usability, this track is a workhorse for media producers. It screams 'inspiration,' 'achievement,' 'adventure,' and 'grandeur.' It's practically tailor-made for corporate videos aiming to inspire confidence or showcase success, high-energy sports montages capturing moments of triumph, or travel content highlighting breathtaking scenery. Film trailers needing an epic, uplifting feel would find this immensely useful, especially for adventure, fantasy, or even dramatic narratives with a hopeful undertone. It could also work effectively in video game menus, cutscenes, or loading screens for titles with similar themes. For advertising, it lends instant scale and emotional impact to product launches, brand stories, or campaigns focused on aspiration and progress. Even podcast intros or outros needing a dose of cinematic flair could benefit. The production quality is clean, well-mixed, and mastered appropriately for broadcast and digital media, ensuring it sits well in a professional production context. It offers that immediate sense of scale and polish that clients often look for.

ImageDescription.value:
Springtime view of the Nestucca Wild and Scenic River at the Fan Creek Recreation Site, Apr. 13, 2018, by Greg Shine, BLM.

The Nestucca River, from its confluence with Ginger Creek downstream to a point near the U.S. Forest Service’s Rocky Bend Recreation Site, was one of several stretches of Oregon rivers to receive wild and scenic river designation through the John D. Dingell, Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act passed by Congress and signed into law by President Donald Trump on March 12, 2019.

This 15.5 mile section of the Nestucca River is a key feature of the larger Nestucca River Recreation Area. The Nestucca River Back Country Byway parallels the wild and scenic river and provides access to recreational activities – including 37 campsites and fishing areas-- at the Alder Glen, Dovre, Fan Creek and Elk Bend Recreation Sites.

Please note that, beginning in mid to late May 2019, the Nestucca Access Road will be temporarily closed for construction between Elk Creek and Davidson pit (gravel section), mile post 12.76 to 15.44. The road will remain closed until the end of October. Detours will use the Bald Mountain and Bible Creek Access Roads. No public access will be allowed during these time periods. Elk Bend campground will be temporarily closed. Alder Glen campground will remain open, accessed only from the west. Fan Creek and Dovre campgrounds will remain open, accessed only from the east. The Upper Nestucca OHV trail system will also remain open during all time periods.

The Nestucca River originates in the northern Oregon Coast Range and flows 50 miles, draining the western slope of range in Yamhill and Tillamook Counties. The river impounded has been near its headwaters to create McGuire Reservoir, the primary water source for the city of McMinnville. The river flows generally west through BLM and USFS administered land, past the communities of Beaver, Hebo, and Cloverdale before entering Nestucca Bay and draining into the Pacific Ocean.

Congress enacted the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act on October 2, 1968, to address the need for a national system of river protection. The WSR Act stipulated that selected rivers should be preserved in a free flowing condition and be protected for the benefit and enjoyment of present and future generations. It seeks to protect and enhance a river’s natural and cultural values and to provide for public use consistent with its free flowing character, water quality, and Oustandingly Remarkable Values (ORVs). A WSR designation affords certain legal protection from development. For instance, new dams cannot be constructed, and Federally-assisted water resource development projects that might negatively affect the designated river values are not permitted within the designated segment.

The Nestucca remains one of the most popular recreation fisheries on Oregon’s North Coast, regularly attracting attention and visitors from outside the region. It is one of the top sport fishing rivers in the state for summer and winter steelhead, and cutthroat trout fishing is also better than average. The fishing along this river includes both drift fishing and bank fishing, with both methods attracting large numbers of both local and out-of-region participants. Due to these factors, recreation values along the Nestucca are outstandingly remarkable.

For more information, visit www.blm.gov/visit/nestucca-river-recreation-area or contact the Northwest Oregon District Office at 503-375-5646.

ObjectName.value: Extracts from the press conference by Massimo D'Alema, Italian Prime Minister, on the timetable of the EU enlargement (L-029493)

Categories.value: Information field template with formatting|Videos of 1999 from Finland|EC-Audiovisual Center review needed|Media from the European Commission|Massimo D'Alema in 1999|Videos by the European Commission|Videos taken on 1999-12-11|1999 European Council in Helsinki

ImageDescription.value: On 11 December 1999, Massimo d'Alema, Italian Prime Ministe, held a national press briefing following the 2-day meeting of the Heads of State or Government of the EU Member States in Helsinki (Finland). The meeting was chaired by Paavo Tapio Lipponen, Finnish Prime Minister, and attended by Romano Prodi, President of the EC. During the press conference, Massimo D'Alema focused on EU enlargement and on the European Defence Policy. He insisted on the Intergovernmental Conference (IGC) as a pre-requisite for EU enlargement. He also explained why, in his opinion, the application of Turkey for EU accession would be an important step for the Mediterranean area, where the country could act as a bridge between the EU and the region, and for Turkey's own democratic transformation. Finally, he evoked the European for Defence. The European Council adopted the 'Millennium declaration', a common strategy on Ukraine and a declaration on Chechnya. It decided to begin accession negotiations with Romania, Slovakia, Latvia, Lithuania, Bulgaria and Malta, and to recognise Turkey as a candidate country, thereby marking a new stage in the enlargement process. It also decided to convene, in February 2000, an intergovernmental conference for revising the Treaties, which was expected to complete its work by December 2000. Other decisions taken were aimed at strengthening the common European security and defence policy, by developing military and civilian crisis management capabilities, with particular emphasis on launching and conducting EU-led military operations in response to international crises. Furthermore, the employment guidelines for 2000 were approved, along with recommendations to the Member States concerning implementation of their employment policies.

ImageDescription.value: On 11 December 1999, António Guterres, Portuguese Prime Minister, held a national press briefing following the 2-day meeting of the Heads of State or Government of the EU Member States in Helsinki (Finland). The meeting was chaired by Paavo Tapio Lipponen, Finnish Prime Minister, and attended by Romano Prodi, President of the EC. During the Portuguese press briefing, António Guterres outlined that they would do their best to start the negotiations with the applicant countries as soon as possible during the Portuguese Presidency. He also recalled that there would be no distinction between previous and new applicant countries and that every negotiation would be according to the merits of the dossier. However he added that no negotiation could start before the fulfillment of the Copenhagen criteria. During their meetings, the European Council adopted the 'Millennium declaration', a common strategy on Ukraine and a declaration on Chechnya. It decided to begin accession negotiations with Romania, Slovakia, Latvia, Lithuania, Bulgaria and Malta, and to recognise Turkey as a candidate country, thereby marking a new stage in the enlargement process. It also decided to convene, in February 2000, an intergovernmental conference for revising the Treaties, which was expected to complete its work by December 2000. Other decisions taken were aimed at strengthening the common European security and defence policy, by developing military and civilian crisis management capabilities, with particular emphasis on launching and conducting EU-led military operations in response to international crises. Furthermore, the employment guidelines for 2000 were approved, along with recommendations to the Member States concerning implementation of their employment policies. ObjectName.value: Extracts from the press conference by Javier Solana, Secretary General of The Council of the EU and High Representative of the CFSP, on the outcome of his visit to Turkey (I-029507)

Categories.value: Information field template with formatting|Videos of 1999 from Finland|Javier Solana in 1999|EC-Audiovisual Center review needed|Media from the European Commission|Videos by the European Commission|Videos taken on 1999-12-11|1999 European Council in Helsinki

ImageDescription.value: On 11 December 1999, Javier Solana, Secretary General of The Council of the EU and High Representative of the Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP), held a press conference following his visit to Ankara (Turkey), the day before. On the first day of the meeting of the European Council, in Helsinki (Finland), the Council recognised Turkey as a candidate country, thereby marking a new stage in the enlargement process. The Council decided to send Javier Solana and Günter Verheugen, Member of the EC in charge of Enlargement, to Ankara, in the evening, to announce its decision to the Turkish Government. Javier Solana reported that they clarified some of the constraints that Turkey might have on the text the Council agreed and which will be approved later. They had two good meetings. He also informed that Turkey would stand beside the other candidate countries with the same criteria as applied to other candidate States, recalling that the only pre-conditions were the Copenhagen criteria. Bülent Ecevit, Turkish Prime Minister, would join the meeting later in the day.

Categories.value: Media from YouTube|Videos from YouTube|License review needed (video)|Uploaded with video2commons|Videos of 2019 from the United States|Videos taken on 2019-06-07|Videos with text in English|Videos in American English|Videos of unidentified people of the United States|Videos by NBC News

ImageDescription.value:
What happens to a forestry community in the aftermath of a disaster? Hurricane Michael - a Category 5 storm - wiped out more than $1 billion worth of timber in the Florida Panhandle when it struck in October 2018, and nearly eight months later the community is still waiting for federal assistance to clean up and replant. The dead trees also mean that the panhandle is facing heightened wildfire risk, as a new hurricane season arrives.

Robby Roberts, a panhandle resident, was playing the long game when he planted his small plot of trees nearly 20 years ago, hoping it would provide him income in his later years. After Hurricane Michael ravaged his land, Roberts, a retiree, was able to sell half his timber for one ninth of the profit that he was expecting. The other half of what was to be his retirement plan now lies on the ground rotting. Roberts, like many other small land owners in the region, must now decide whether to reinvest in a crop that will take 20 years to see a return.

ImageDescription.value: The first Multi-Role Tanker Transport (MRTT) aircraft procured by NATO and the European Defence Agency (EDA) arrived at its main operating base in Eindhoven, the Netherlands, on Tuesday, 30 June 2020. The aircraft is part of the Multinational Multirole Tanker and Transport Fleet (MMF), which will boost participating Allies’ ability to quickly respond to emergencies in multiple domains, including medical evacuation. The fleet consists of eight Airbus A330 MRTT aircraft, which will be delivered between 2020 and 2024, and is managed by the NATO Support and Procurement Agency (NSPA). It provides Belgium, the Czech Republic, Germany, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Norway with strategic tanker and transport capabilities. This project will substantially increase European capacity in air-to-air refuelling, and is an example of effective cooperation between NATO and the European Union in the delivery of critical defence capabilities. Sharing resources enables participating nations to get access to state-of-the-art capabilities that would be difficult or impossible to procure individually. Footage includes shots of the MRTT aircraft arriving and landing at the Eindhoven airport, shots of the aircraft’s Commander and crew, shots inside the aircraft and various external shots of the aircraft.

Title: Ham and the Jitney Bus

Genre: comedy, Ham and Bud-series
Running time: 12:18
Synopsis:

A short comic film in which a bickering duo start a taxi company. A constantly quarrelling duo, consisting of a tall fat man and a short thin man, find a wallet on the street, with twenty dollars inside. They use that money to buy a car, and then set up their own taxi company. The competition is fierce, and their clumsiness creates many problems. ObjectName.value: Getting submarines talking to airplanes, finally

Categories.value: Media from YouTube|Videos of 2018|Uploaded with video2commons|License reviewed by YouTubeReviewBot|Underwater technology

ImageDescription.value:
Until recently, there has never been a way to send communication signals between air and water. If an underwater submarine passes beneath a plane in the sky, there's been no way for them to communicate with each other without having the submarine surface, jeopardizing its location to an adversary. Fadel Adib and Francesco Tonolini of MIT Media Lab have developed a way to connect these seemingly dissonant mediums through something called Translational Acoustic-RF communication, or TARF. Using sound waves from underwater, and radar from the air, messages can be transmitted by creating faint ripples on the surface of the water.

Professor: Fadel Adib Student author: Francesco Tonolini Student Collaborator: JunSu Jang Video Producer: Jimmy Day

More information at: tarf.media.mit.edu

Categories.value: Metro Cammell Glasgow Subway rolling stock|Buchanan Street subway station|Flickr images reviewed by trusted users|Flickr images missing SDC creator|Flickr images missing SDC inception|Flickr images missing SDC source of file|Videos of 2015 from the United Kingdom|PD-author-FlickrPDM|August 2015 in Glasgow|August 2015 in rail transport in Scotland|Videos of trains in Scotland|Videos of rapid transit|Videos of Glasgow Subway

ImageDescription.value:
It seems that whenever we visit a new place that has an underground railway system we just have to try it!


Glasgow's is actually a bit of a gem. Firstly, it's really, really old. It started operation in 1896(!) making it the third oldest underground railway system in the world. It's about six miles long and the route hasn't changed since it opened all those decades ago.


Other oddities. It runs completely underground which is unusual. It's so old that it uses a non standard gauge, being 4ft rather than the 'standard' 4' 8.5" and it has teeny tiny tunnels only 11 feet across meaning that the trains are also really tiny. If you're very tall you won't be able to stand upright in the cars.


I'm also delighted to report that the trains are largely orange, and we like orange metro trains. :) It was great fun, and a good one to try.

ImageDescription.value: On 21 February 1999, EU Ministers for Foreign Affairs gathered in Luxembourg. The meeting was chaired by Joschka Fischer, German Federal Minister for Foreign Affairs. The objective of the Conclave’s deliberations was to draw initial orientations in order to steer further negotiations in view of the informal meeting of Heads of State and Government in Petersberg (Germany) on 26 February 1999. Following the meeting, George Papandreou, Greek Minister for Foreign Affairs, held a press conference. he focused on the Kurdish issue and the Greece/Turkey relations on this matter. ImageDescription.value:
G-GBTV, is an AS355N Écureuil 2, also known as the Twin Squirrel and TwinStar. It is a twin-engine light utility helicopter operated by GB Helicopters and owned by Cheshire Helicopters Ltd.
G-GBTV was originally manufactured in 1999, with the serial number 5360, by Aérospatiale, later Eurocopter, now Airbus Helicopters. Its home base (at 2025), is Elstree Aerodrome (EGTR), in Hertfordshire, England.
The helicopter can hold up to 5 passengers (4 rear seats, 1 front seat beside the pilot), with seating configuration of a forward-facing bench-style. It has a cruise speed of approximately 120 knots (138 mph), and a range of approximately 395 nautical miles (731 km). Operational roles include VIP charter flights across the UK, aerial filming, load-lifting operations and infrastructure inspections. In 2021, G-GBTV received a jet-black paint livery, while sometimes with added advertising idents. In the video it is seen flying over north London on 23 May 2025

ImageDescription.value: Animated zoom on the cornea of a high-resolution photographic subject. The zoom begins with a passport photo-style framing of the subject, and ends with a full face close-up of a bystander captured in the subject's corneal reflection. Successive movie frames represent a linear magnification of 6%. Each frame was resized to 720 pixels wide ×540 pixels high using bicubic interpolation to reduce high spatial frequency noise. Contrast was enhanced separately for each frame using the Auto Contrast function in Adobe Photoshop to improve definition. The image sequence was then converted to movie format for viewing.

ImageDescription.value: A movie file illustrating stable subpleural alveoli in the normal rat lung during dynamic tidal ventilation. Each sphere-shaped object is an inflated individual alveolus and there is minimal atelectasis (that is, the entire field is covered by inflated alveoli). Notice there is minimal alveolar movement (that is, alveoli are stable) during tidal ventilation, at least in the two dimensions that can be seen with our in vivo microscope technique.

Credit.value: Pavone L, Albert S, Carney D, Gatto L, Halter J, Nieman G (2007). "Injurious mechanical ventilation in the normal lung causes a progressive pathologic change in dynamic alveolar mechanics". Critical Care. DOI:10.1186/cc5940. PMID 17565688. PMC: 2206429.

ImageDescription.value: A movie file demonstrating unstable subpleural alveoli in the injured rat lung during dynamic tidal ventilation. The red area without alveoli (that is, individual circles) shows diffuse atelectasis prior to inspiration. The individual alveoli (spheres) 'pop' open with inspiration and then quickly collapse with expiration. Notice that alveoli are very unstable and there is complete collapse of most alveoli during deflation and than reinflation during lung inflation – classic alveolar recruitment/derecruitment.

Credit.value: Pavone L, Albert S, Carney D, Gatto L, Halter J, Nieman G (2007). "Injurious mechanical ventilation in the normal lung causes a progressive pathologic change in dynamic alveolar mechanics". Critical Care. DOI:10.1186/cc5940. PMID 17565688. PMC: 2206429.

ImageDescription.value: The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) launched a new cargo vehicle, the HTV-X1, to the International Space Station on Oct. 25, U.S. time, atop an H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan. Loaded with more than four tons of food and supplies for the Expedition 73 crew, HTV-X1 will arrive at the station on Oct. 29 where it will be robotically captured by the station’s Canadarm2 robot arm operated by JAXA astronaut Kimiya Yui and mechanically installed on the Earth-facing port of the Harmony module for a three-month stay.

ImageDescription.value: art002m1200912233C (April 1, 2026) - The darkened interior of the Orion spacecraft is suddenly illuminated when the spacecraft’s launch abort system is jettisoned 3 minutes and 18 seconds after the launch of Artemis II on April 1, 2026. The launch abort system, which would pull Orion and its crew to safety in the event of an emergency during launch, provides a protective shroud for the Orion crew module during the dynamic early portion of ascent. When it is no longer needed, it is jettisoned, exposing the spacecraft windows to sunlight for the first time in the mission. This view comes from a camera looking over the shoulders of Artemis II Commander Reid Wiseman and Pilot Victor Glover.

ObjectName.value: James Guthrie's Home Movies of Tibet (1945) - extract

Categories.value: Media from YouTube|PD India|1945 in Tibet|License review needed (video)|YouTube videos review needed|Arranged license review project|Files with archived source and marked for license review|Videos of 2008|Uploaded with video2commons|PD-old missing SDC copyright status|Videos from Tibet|Videos of Tenzin Gyatso, 14th Dalai Lama|James Guthrie (physician)|Tenzin Gyatso, 14th Dalai Lama in 1945

ImageDescription.value:
Highlights from the BFI National Archive's extensive collection of films shot in Tibet prior to the Chinese occupation can now be seen in the BBC/BFI co-production, 'The Lost World of Tibet' (2008). Featuring a potent interview with the Dalai Lama an extended version the documentary is available to buy on DVD from the BFI Filmstore - http://filmstore.bfi.org.uk/acatalog/info_7836.html

This film includes a rare close-up of the young Dalai Lama being carried along in his golden palanquin.

This amateur film was made by Major (later Lieutenant-Colonel) James Guthrie who held the post of Medical Officer in Gyantse from 1934 to 1936 and Civil Surgeon of Bhutan and Tibet from 1945 to 1948. He was accompanied by his wife, Joan, during the second tour of duty. The post was primarily to ensure the health of members of the Diplomatic Mission in Lhasa but medical services were also made available to Tibetans and regular clinics were held in Lhasa and the surrounding countryside.

Major Guthrie did much to overcome local resistance to western medicine and such was his acceptance that he was entrusted to remove a cyst from the Dalai Lama's peacock as well as advise on many other medical conditions amongst the local populace. (Jan Faull)

All titles on the BFI Films channel are preserved in the vast collections of the BFI National Archive. To find out more about the Archive visit http://www.bfi.org.uk/archive-collections

ImageDescription.value: The third and final main engine has been installed on Space Shuttle Discovery at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The engines will provide part of the driving force for the Space Shuttle on its Return to Flight mission to the International Space Station. 'Behind me, what we're seeing today is the installation of the third engine on the Discovery vehicle. That's a major milestone for NASA on Return to Flight.' Among the three engines, one is making its fifth space flight, one is making its third, and one is flying for the very first time on the mission, which is targeted for May's launch planning window. Weighing in at just over 7,000 pounds each, the Space Shuttle Main Engines are the largest reusable liquid rocket engines in the world. During liftoff, they use up more than half a million gallons of fuel and generate as much energy as 23 Hoover Dams. The Boeing Company's Rocketdyne Propulsion and Power Division builds the engines for NASA. 'We're very proud to accomplish that milestone for NASA, which is going to lead us on Return to Flight, and we'll be very proud to be there.' Returning the Space Shuttle to flight is the first step in NASA's Vision for Space Exploration, which calls for man to return to the Moon, then on to Mars and beyond.

ImageDescription.value: COMMENTATOR: And Discovery now on take off roll, atop a 747 Shuttle Carrier Aircraft, just about to begin the first leg of its return back to the Kennedy Space Center. And the ferry flight of Discovery underway, the first stop again planned to be Altus Air Force Base in South Western Oklahoma. It's about a 3-hour trip from, from California to Altus Air Force Base. It would be a refueling stop, weather permitting, a couple of hour refueling stop and then the next leg will take Discovery from Altus Air Force Base to an overnight stopover at Barksdale Air force Base in Central Western Louisiana. The actual, the operational altitude for a ferry flight with a shuttle on its back is 15,000 feet. The 747 actually is led by about a 100 miles out in front by a KC-135 aircraft which basically flies weather reconnaissance.

ObjectName.value: Jsc2026m000047 How To Train For The Moon (jsc2026m000047 How To Train For The Moon)

Categories.value: PD NASA|Uploaded with video2commons|NASA videos in 2026|Files from NASA with known IDs|NASA Library files uploaded by OptimusPrimeBot|Artemis 2 training

ImageDescription.value: Before the Artemis II crew journeys to the Moon inside the Orion spacecraft, they will spend countless hours practicing every aspect of their mission. At NASA’s Johnson Space Center, the Artemis II crew trains inside Orion simulators to practice procedures, troubleshoot malfunctions, and work through realistic mission scenarios. This training ensures the astronauts and flight control team are ready to operate Orion’s systems and respond to any challenge during the 10-day flight. From learning the fundamentals of Orion’s life support systems to conducting integrated simulations with flight controllers, every training session helps ensure mission success. Using Johnson’s full-scale Orion mockup in the Space Vehicle Mockup Facility and simulators like the Orion Mission Simulator and the Beta Dome, the crew is prepared for any scenario they may encounter aboard Orion during Artemis II. This is how to train for the Moon. Credit: NASA Writer: Erika Peters Editor: Phil Sexton Producers: Rad Sinyak, Erika Peters

ImageDescription.value: Four Artemis II astronauts just returned from their journey around the Moon, but preparations to land humans on the surface of the Moon once again have been in progress long before liftoff. Follow NASA astronaut Victor Glover as he arrives at the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas, to put on his spacesuit and begin an underwater run in the training pool. This day-in-the-life snapshot depicts a simulated traverse on the lunar surface, including using lunar geology tools, recovering from a fall, and more. Glover, and many other astronauts, participate in these simulations to help crew trainers develop lesson plans that future moonwalkers will use in training. This video was filmed in August 2023.

ImageDescription.value:
These videos show how technicians at NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans installed the third and fourth RS-25 engines onto the core stage for the agency’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket that will help power NASA’s first crewed Artemis mission to the Moon.

Technicians added the first engine to the SLS core stage Sept. 11. The second engine was installed onto the stage Sept. 15 with the third and fourth engines following Sept. 19 and Sept. 20. Engineers consider the engines to be “soft” mated to the rocket stage. Technicians with NASA, Aerojet Rocketdyne, an L3Harris Technologies company and the RS-25 engines lead contractor, along with Boeing, the core stage lead contractor, will now focus efforts on the complex tax of fully securing the engines to the stage and integrating the propulsion and electrical systems within the structure.

NASA is working to land the first woman and first person of color on the Moon under Artemis. SLS is part of NASA’s backbone for deep space exploration, along with Orion and the Gateway in orbit around the Moon. SLS is the only rocket that can send Orion, astronauts, and supplies to the Moon in a single mission.

ObjectName.value: Machining NICER’s Patches (SVS14610 - Machine Shop B-roll - Part 1)

Categories.value: PD NASA|NICER|Video display resolution 3840 x 2160|NASA videos in 2024|NASA SVS files uploaded by OptimusPrimeBot

ImageDescription.value: This video shows Richard Koenecke, an engineer at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center, creating the body of one of the NICER (Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer) patches.0:00 Two blocks of aluminum sit on a counter in front of a laptop that displays the schematics for the NICER patches. 0:06 Koenecke puts one block on the bed of a saw littered with metal shavings and then trims the block. 0:23 Koenecke sands down the block’s rough edges. 0:30 Koenecke walks into another part of his workshop. 0:37 Koenecke preps the machining chamber. 0:49 Inside the chamber, the machine starts to carve out the shape of the patch. Fluid sprayed from the nozzles above the tool helps cool the metal. 0:56 Koenecke looks into the chamber. 0:59 The chamber is shown at different angles. 1:15 Koenecke walking up to the chamber window. 1:22 Inside the chamber, the patch’s shape is now visible amidst a sea of aluminum shavings. 1:25 The cutting tool refines the shape of the patch. 1:40 Koenecke looks at a computer readout for the machining chamber. 1:45 Inside the chamber, the cutting tool lowers to hollow out the patch. 1:56 Koenecke holds and turns a block of the aluminum. 2:45 Koenecke’s dog Sara guards his shop on the Eastern Shore. 2:53 Koenecke sands a block of aluminum. 3:01 He closes the doors to the machining chamber and adjusts the settings on a computer screen. 3:10 Numbers change on the chamber’s computer screen. 3:31 Koenecke holds and turns the fully machined patch body. 3:51 In slow motion, Koenecke walking through his shop. 4:25 In slow motion, Koenecke holds the patch in close-up shots.Credit: NASA/Sophia Roberts and Scott Wiessinger

Artist.value: NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio - Advocates in Manpower Management, Inc./Sophia Roberts, KBR Wyle Services, LLC/Scott Wiessinger, University of Maryland College Park/Jeanette Kazmierczak, ADNET Systems, Inc./Aaron E. Lepsch

ObjectName.value: Machining NICER’s Patches (SVS14610 - Machine Shop B-roll Part 2 Slow Motion)

Categories.value: PD NASA|NICER|Video display resolution 3840 x 2160|NASA videos in 2024|Videos of metalworking|NASA SVS files uploaded by OptimusPrimeBot

ImageDescription.value: This slow-motion video compilation shows Richard Koenecke working on a NICER patch in his machine shop.0:00 Pan along the main machining chamber’s computer screen. 0:03 Koenecke watches the chamber as the cutter inside begins to shape a patch from a block of aluminum. 0:18 Koenecke’s hand makes an adjustment on the chamber’s computer. 0:26 Koenecke cleans up a partially machined patch inside the chamber. 0:42 Outside of the machining chamber hangs a clipboard with a schematic of the NICER patch. 0:50 The camera’s focus gradually shifts from the outside to the inside of the chamber. 1:03 Inside the chamber, the mill begins to hollow out the patch. 1:23 Numbers fluctuate on the chamber computer. 1:33 Koenecke holds the hollowed patch. 1:54 Koenecke enters the shop.Credit: NASA/Sophia Roberts and Scott Wiessinger

Текст песни:


Мы все планируем уехать

И храним коробки на балконе

Но никуда не уезжаем

Может когда-нибудь потом?


Прощание с декадансом

Вокруг так много контента

Которым можно упарываться

Зачем делать что-то еще?


Усыпляет информация

Я просто хочу разобраться


Нам предлагают разделить

Великие достижения культуры

И закрыть глаза на тот факт

Что у нас своей собственной жизни не будет


Ведь это слишком сложные квесты для млекопитающих

Таких как мы

И если бы был хоть какой-то смысл

Мы бы давно его отыскали


Мы бы подготовились

Мы бы сдали экзамен

Нет проверяющих

Билетов и правил

Если бы смысл был

Мы бы давно его уже отыскали


——


Надежда стреляется в живот

Было увлекательно

Но стало тяжело

Ноябрь хватает за горло

И не дает дышать

Рассказы медленно подходят к концу


Мы плывем в нашей лодке

Мы плывем в нашей лодке

Мы плывем и молчим

ImageDescription.value:
Текст песни:


Полетишь ли ты со мною на ракете falcon

через 20 лет осваивать Марс

ответ нужен прямо сейчас.


Поезд уходит в подсознание

со скоростью 200 километров в час

И кончились те обстоятельства

Что делали нас друзьями.


Мне говорили:

ты к драматизации склонна

и часто делаешь сама

из мухи слона

А по моему это вы упрощаете в конец

Жизнь, увиденная через призму страданий

Без какого либо глубинного подтекста


Как гора заканчивается под небесами

И на вершине стоящий крест

Приглашает меня в путешествие

Еле уловимыми жестами.


Я не пускаю новых людей в свою жизнь

мне кажется все они

напечатаны на 3d принтере!



Называют пессимизмом,

то что по сути реализм.


Рациональность и прагматизм

Не дадут мне скатиться вниз.


Люди выращенные в условиях теплиц

будут удивляться крайне

когда столкнутся с тем

что счастье не входило в планы мироздания.


Культура дает мне указания:

пока в одном городе с тобою

кто-то голодает на вокзале

или прыгает вниз головой с моста

ты не будешь радоваться.


Природа так эгоистична

мы добры только к своим близким


но чтобы увидеть и понять -

страдание везде одинаково

надо выбраться из раковины.


Беспокойства много не бывает

люди продолжают застревать

на железнодорожных переездах


как будто нет другого времени и места

не хотела б я быть машинистом

такая ответственность



работать за гроши

вот на что потратится жизнь

вот для чего вы ползете на работу

с мужеством поливальных машин


эволюционируй или умри это просто бизнес

ничего личного

ничего лишнего


накапливанье денег

чтобы побороть животный страх

красные цифры на черном циферблате

И две мигающие точки


Мир внутри меня постарел и упростился

Сложился как карточный домик

А есть ли жизнь в 30?

А есть ли жизнь в 40?


С тех пор как водили за ручку в музыкальную школу

и звездное небо меня потрясало

многое изменилось

на каждое хочу приходится по десять надо


Кидаю душу в микроволновку

мне провели операцию на глазах

но лучше б сделали пластику души

ее надо к чертовой матери ушить


я не пускаю новых людей в свою жизнь

мне кажется все они напечатаны

на 3d принтере!


Расскажи мне историю

Интересную страшную разную

Расскажи мне историю

Но обо мне никому не рассказывай

Возле тебя я заряжаюсь на все хорошее

Как телефон подпитываюсь от беспроводной зарядки

Я приму таблетку и запью водою,

день забрали, предстоят другие

можно водку пить,

но это еще никому не помогало.


Как сойти с орбиты,

не сойдя с дистанции?

я знакома с будущим, и мне оно не нравится,

Как приготовить ужин, не нарезав пальцы?


Я не пускаю новых людей в свою жизнь

мне кажется все они напечатаны

на чудовищном 3d принтере



Я приглашаю тебя в путешествие

Еле уловимыми жестами

Не назад, но только вперед

И все что увидишь - твое.

Все что захочешь - твое.


Полетишь ли со мною на ракете falcon

Через 20 лет осваивать Марс?

Ответ нужен сейчас.

ImageDescription.value: Behavior of a monopolar RCC1 bead spindle. Two side-by-side fluorescence time-lapse movies of egg extract spindle assembly reactions containing rhodamine labeled tubulin and beads coated with RCC1 plus kinesin-1 motor domain, shown over the same time interval of 37 min. ObjectName.value: Motor Cortical Representation of Hand Translation and Rotation

Categories.value: Ogv videos|Video display resolution 640 x 480|Videos of neurosciences|Videos of motor control

ImageDescription.value:
This movie shows actual hand kinematics for the 3D center-out with rotation task in the virtual reality simulator, as well as simultaneous recording of spikes for a motor cortical neuron
 that  encodes both hand translation and rotation in a nonlinear fashion. The subject's 3D hand position and hand orientation in the frontal plane were mapped directly to the position and orientation of the orange cursor in the virtual reality simulator.  The preferred translational direction of this neuron is right, backward, and up.    It prefers counter-clockwise rotation.    This movie shows a subset (12 movements) of this neuron’s data.    In the actual experiment, all movements were performed in random order.    In this movie, those movements were reordered so that all three movements with the  same translation direction but different rotations  were grouped together.

ObjectName.value: Miniature-Effect Drone View Exeter Rowing Club

Categories.value: CC-Zero|Buildings in Exeter|Self-published work|Drone videos from England|Tilt-shift videos

ImageDescription.value: This video captures the charming front buildings adjacent to the Exeter Rowing Club, as seen from a drone flying to the right. The video employs a zoomed-in effect that cleverly mimics the look of a miniature model, a technique often referred to as the tilt-shift effect. This visual trickery renders the scene with enhanced depth and brings an almost storybook quality to the buildings and surrounding environment. The architecture, with its varied facades and the natural backdrop, becomes part of a seemingly tiny, crafted world. The people walking by, appearing as diminutive figures, contribute to the illusion of a small-scale tableau. This frame is from a video that showcases not only the technical prowess of drone filming but also the creative possibilities of post-production effects to alter our perception of scale and space.

ObjectName.value: Movie 7. Comparison between directed (motor) movement and diffusive movement

Categories.value: Molecular dynamics simulation|Self-published work

ImageDescription.value: A "hypothetical" motor moves along a cytoskeleton in a speed of 1 micro-m/sec. The orange spot moves randomly with a diffusion constant of 10 micro-m^2/sec, which is a typical diffusion constant for proteins inside the cell. The orange gradient reflects the average concentration of the orange spot diffusing from the center of the image. You can see from the movie that diffusion can reach farther in a short period of time, but in a longer time scale, the directed movement wins.

ImageDescription.value:
Audio recording of a steam engine made by Fenton, Murray and Wood of Holbeck, Leeds, around 1805, and said to be the third-oldest working steam engine in the world. Used by John Bradley & Co of Stourbridge from 1805-1931, and from 1931-1961 by N Hingkey & Sons of Netherton. Now in Thinktank, Birmingham.
We hear engine started from cold. First, steam is allowed through the cylinders, their drain cocks open, to warm them. The flywheel is rotated by hand, to set the engine in motion, and the recording ends with the engine ticking over at low speed, with one "clunk" per revolution.

ImageDescription.value: The asteroid redirect vehicle demonstrates the “gravity tractor” planetary defense technique on a hazardous-size asteroid. The gravity tractor method leverages the mass of the spacecraft to impart a gravitational force on the asteroid, slowly altering the asteroid’s trajectory. The demonstration is conducted after capturing the boulder and is referred to as the “enhanced gravity tractor” because the additional mass of the boulder enhances the force that can be transmitted to the asteroid.
